To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: URGENT: Check your Brightline 6% developer – batch LX2291

Hi everyone,

Please check your Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer 1L bottles before you use any more. Kelvin Trade has said there’s been a filling error and batch LX2291 may actually contain 12% (40 vol).

The batch code is on the BASE OF THE BOTTLE, not the box. Please check every bottle, including open ones in your trolley as well as any stock in the back. The affected batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November. Kelvin Trade says other batches and other strengths aren’t affected.

If you’ve got LX2291, stop using it immediately. Keep it separate so nobody picks it up by mistake. The rep is in on Tuesday and you can hand bottles back to him, or take them to the Hillington depot for a full credit.

If you’ve had a problem with a bottle, please keep it back and don’t bin it. Keep the supplier email and make a note of what happened, including the date, product and batch. Take dated photos where appropriate. That bottle may be needed as evidence, so don’t hand it back until you’ve checked what’s needed for any incident or insurance claim.

What to look out for

I used a new bottle from this batch on Saturday for a bleach retouch. The hair lifted much faster than usual and the client felt burning. I rinsed it off, but she was left with a red, sore patch on her scalp.

Aileen also had foils get really hot on Thursday and the hair lifted much faster than expected. She’d thought it might have been the heater, but her bottle is LX2291 too. The result was brassy and patchy.

So please watch out for unusually fast lift, excess heat, burning or discomfort, and uneven or brassy results. Those are things we’ve seen, but please don’t use the batch even if it seems fine.

If someone reacts in the chair

Stop the service straight away. For a suspected chemical burn, call 999 immediately – don’t wait for blisters or severe pain. Put on gloves and carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible. Rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about an hour, and follow the call handler’s instructions. Don’t use shampoo, creams or other chemicals. Chemical burns need hospital assessment.

Call 999 immediately for breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse too. Once the person is being looked after, record what happened in the incident book at the desk.

The salon’s first-aid reference is here if you need it: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/acid-and-chemical-burns/

Please check today and let anyone else who buys from the rep know. This is more than an inconvenience – someone has been hurt, and I don’t want it happening to anyone else.

Kirsty
